identity.title: Air Permit Annual Report for 2025 (Standard ACDP 26-2841-ST-01) with Oregon DEQ Receipt Confirmation, Portland Facility
identity.issuer: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC (report signed by Daniel Okafor, Plant Manager); receipt confirmation from the Oregon DEQ Air Quality Program (page 1)

scan.summary: This is your annual report on the Portland air permit for calendar year 2025, filed under Condition 4.1, plus DEQ's email confirming it was received on February 12, 2026. It is proof that the report was filed on time and a record of 2025 operations: throughput, the scrubber logs, C-1 carbon replacement, and one deviation that was reported. DEQ says plainly that the email confirms receipt only. It does not mean DEQ found the report complete or found the facility meeting its permit.
scan.freshness_note: This covers 2025, the most recent full reporting year, so it is the current report. The 2026 report will be due early in 2027 (the exact due date is in your permit, not in this document). One date in the report has already passed: it says the C-1 carbon was due for replacement by March 14, 2026. Check that the replacement record exists.

gaps.title: Confirm the C-1 carbon was replaced by March 14, 2026
gaps.description: The report says the next C-1 carbon replacement was due on or before March 14, 2026. That date passed more than six months ago. Nothing in this document shows it was done, and no replacement record for 2026 is in your files.
gaps.fix: Find the 2026 carbon replacement record (vendor invoice or service ticket, date, carbon type and amount) and keep it with the permit records. If the carbon was not replaced on time, read Condition 3.3 and the deviation-reporting conditions (5.1/5.2) in the permit and decide whether DEQ needs to be told.
gaps.citation: Standard ACDP 26-2841-ST-01, Condition 3.3 (as named in the report; the permit's exact wording was not checked here)
gaps.quote: The next scheduled replacement is on or before March 14, 2026.

deadlines.title: Replace the carbon in unit C-1 (yearly schedule, according to the report)
deadlines.source_line: The next scheduled replacement is on or before March 14, 2026.

deadlines.title: Keep this confirmation and the permit records for five years (inferred: February 2031 counted from receipt)
deadlines.source_line: Records required by the permit must be kept for five years and made available to the Department on request.

deadlines.title: File the annual report for 2026 under Condition 4.1 (due date is set in the permit, not stated here)
deadlines.source_line: Submitted under Condition 4.1 · Period: January 1 to December 31, 2025

facts.affects: Sets the reporting, monitoring and record-keeping conditions for the Portland site.

facts.value: Acid line S-1 (hydrochloric, sulfuric, nitric acid solutions): 1,842,000 lb over 238 days in 2025. Caustic line S-2 (sodium and potassium hydroxide solutions): 1,210,000 lb over 231 days.
facts.quote: hydrochloric, sulfuric and nitric acid solutions
facts.affects: Volumes this large of listed acids may trigger EPCRA Tier II and TRI (Form R) reporting.

facts.value: Tanks T-3 to T-6 hold acetone, isopropanol, toluene and xylene, vented through C-1. 3,960,000 gallons received in 2025.
facts.affects: Toluene and xylene at this volume matter for TRI, flammable-liquid fire code rules and Tier II.

facts.value: Carbon last replaced March 14, 2025 (Calgon Filtrasorb 400, 1,800 lb, Northwest Carbon Services). Outlet checked weekly by detector tube; no breakthrough in 2025.
facts.quote: The carbon in C-1 was replaced on March 14, 2025 (Calgon Filtrasorb 400, 1,800 pounds, by Northwest Carbon Services).
facts.affects: Sets the yearly carbon replacement cycle. Spent carbon may also need a hazardous-waste determination.

facts.value: One deviation: S-2 recirculation pump failed August 22, 2025. DEQ notified August 23; written report sent September 2 (DEV-2025-0913).
facts.quote: The Department was notified by email on August 23, 2025 and a written report was submitted on September 2, 2025
facts.affects: This is the site's deviation history, which DEQ may look at during inspections or permit renewal.

The report looks internally consistent: days logged match operating days, and zero days fell outside the 2.0–6.0 in. w.c. range. This review did not check the report against the permit's own condition wording, and DEQ has not said the report is complete. The 2026 due date and the five-year retention end date were worked out, not read. The March 14, 2026 carbon item comes from a date that has passed with no record in your files. It is not a defect in the report itself.

Quarterly inspections under Condition 3.2 were carried out on March 27, June 26, September 25 and
December 18, 2025, and are recorded in the scrubber maintenance file.
3. Carbon adsorption unit C-1 (Condition 3.3)
The carbon in C-1 was replaced on March 14, 2025 (Calgon Filtrasorb 400, 1,800 pounds, by Northwest
Carbon Services). Weekly detector-tube checks at the C-1 outlet were carried out every week in 2025 with
no breakthrough detected. The next scheduled replacement is on or before March 14, 2026.
4. Deviations and excess emissions (Conditions 5.1 and 5.2)
One deviation. On August 22, 2025 the S-2 recirculation pump failed at 14:10; the caustic repackaging
line was stopped within four minutes and remained down until the pump was replaced on August 24. No
product was repackaged on the caustic line while the scrubber was out of service. The Department was
notified by email on August 23, 2025 and a written report was submitted on September 2, 2025 (DEQ
reference DEV-2025-0913).
Opacity: no visible emissions above 20 percent were observed at any permitted source in 2025.
I certify that the information in this report is true, accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge.
Daniel Okafor, Plant Manager · Signed: February 10, 2026
